automatedCases.expected: Archive extraction is byte-for-byte and metadata equivalent to the selected sources.
Zero-byte files and empty directories are preserved.
Unicode, spaces, and punctuation in names are preserved.
Nested relative paths remain inside the restore root.
All block-boundary files survive archive and restore without truncation.
Same-content files remain distinct by path.
A valid archive restores and compares successfully.
Compressed archive is smaller and restores the original SHA-256.
Pseudo-random content archives and restores without data loss.
Encrypted archive restores with the test password and does not expose known plaintext.
Include and exclude path rules have the expected path set.
File type presets select the expected sample extensions.
Name, wildcard, and case examples match the documented behavior.
Relative and explicit time ranges include the expected fixtures.
Size threshold boundaries include only the expected fixtures.
Files owned by the current user are selected.
Preview selection equals the restored path set for combined filters.
A due scheduled job is started once and its next-run time advances.
Repeated run requests coalesce and removed jobs do not rerun.
A missing monitored directory is reopened and requests a full rescan when restored.
Restored metadata and ACL match where the current account has permission.
A safe relative symbolic link is preserved without following it.
The production remote client uploads a snapshot over local HTTPS and the server lists it.
A second user cannot probe or read the first user's chunks or snapshots.
A local encrypted snapshot restores to the same paths and SHA-256 values.
An unchanged second snapshot reuses existing content-addressed blocks.
A small in-file change creates a recoverable second snapshot without losing the first.
First/last block, mtime-only, and attribute-only changes are reflected in restore.
Pruning retains the requested latest snapshots and does not remove referenced chunks.
After server interruption, retry uploads only missing chunks and commits one complete snapshot.
Remote restore resumes from verified cached chunks and produces matching file hashes.
